note: P4353 (Pro 29:20) — a man hasty in words? there is more hope for a fool than for him.

dims.v: rash speech — the man who speaks before he thinks, worse than a fool
the man who is hasty in his words — rash, unconsidered speech that blurts before thinking, a fault so deep there is more hope for a fool than for him
the fool he is set below (266836)
set against the fool who has more hope than he

uts (hasten/press) — 'do you see a man who is HASTY in his words? there is more hope for a fool than for him' (cf 26:12); rash speech is worse than folly, for it forecloses the reflection by which even a fool might learn. Emergent: hastiness of tongue as a near-incurable fault.
teachable folly — with more hope than the hasty-tongued
the fool who, for all his folly, has more hope than the man hasty in words — because folly may yet learn where rash, thoughtless speech leaves no room to
the hasty-tongued he is set above (266833)
set against the hasty in words who has even less hope

kesil (fool) — 'there is more hope for a FOOL than for him'; even the fool is better placed than the man of rash tongue, for the fool may yet pause and learn. Thoughtless haste is worse than plain folly.
